notes.text: The divorce deed is discussed in the final chapter of Yevamot, near the beginning of folio 116a. The deed’s quoted name is bare.
The checked wording distinguishes Sura as the place of the instrument and Nehardea as the man’s designation. The witnesses in the case do not establish his identity with the other appearance.
The document from Shemuel’s court explicitly gives Anan bar Ḥiyya and Ḥanan bar Rabbah as cross-attesting witnesses. Heilprin keeps his alternate spelling Rava.
Geniva introduces a separate tradition of Rav Ḥanan bar Rava in Gittin. The Ketubot attestation itself names Shemuel, and the adjacent Heilprin Ḥanan headword treats these as distinct events.
Do not turn the compressed Geniva appendage into a second judge of the attestation. Compare Ketubot and the reciprocal Heilprin headword.
